summary: Pipelines can hard-code a bad decomposition, amplify handoff loss, and turn model uncertainty into a brittle distributed system whose apparent determinism exceeds its actual reliability.

points.text: Information omitted from an upstream artifact cannot be recovered by a downstream specialist; repeated summarization and schema coercion can systematically erase caveats.
Parallel agents may write against stale shared state or produce mutually incompatible patches. A final merge node cannot reliably resolve conflicts it was not given evidence to understand.
Retry policies can repeat non-idempotent tool effects, while permissive loops consume budget without improving the answer. Durable orchestration does not make side effects safe by itself.
A fixed pipeline can underperform one capable agent on novel tasks while adding latency, inference cost, trace volume, and maintenance burden.
